title: Entra ID enterprise application permissions blade — requested delegated scopes at consent time
event_type: Entra ID enterprise application registration — consent-prompt scope detail (admin/user view)

fields.label: Admin consent required
fields.value: No — user consent allowed under current tenant policy

callouts.explanation: An unverified or newly-registered publisher domain is the strongest visual cue at consent time that the app is not from a known vendor, but the blade presents it with no more visual weight than any other field, so users skim past it.
Mail.Read and Files.ReadWrite.All are the broad delegated scopes that give a consented app standing read/write access to the victim's mailbox and files, not a one-time action.
offline_access is the specific scope that converts a single consent into a long-lived refresh token — this is what keeps the app's access working after the victim resets their password.

When this is 'No,' any individual user completing the consent prompt grants the scope tenant-wide for their own account with no administrator review, which is the exact gap illicit-consent-grant attacks rely on.

note: Illustrative and conceptual — a reconstructed field breakdown of what the consent blade shows, not a captured screenshot of any real Entra ID tenant or vendor console UI.
